title: The tutor
summary: An assistant for the whole app that builds courses and lessons and manages them through tools.
description: With an OpenRouter key and a model, the Tutor tab is an assistant that acts in the app through tools.

stories.as: a learner who knows what they need Polish for
stories.want: to ask for a course in plain words and have it built
stories.soThat: I never assemble lessons by hand

stories.want: to leave the app while the tutor works
stories.soThat: a long reply does not hold me up

requirements.text: The tutor needs a model that supports tool calling; Settings marks the models that do.
The tutor can create a course on a theme as a path: the conversation first, then word and sentence drills with study lessons between, listening after, and a writing lesson last.
The tutor can create a single lesson of every type except a dialogue, which is made as part of a course, and can list, read, update, delete, move, reorder and reschedule lessons.
The tutor can change any open course, the demo included, and delete any course; a closed course can only be deleted.
The tutor can have songs and podcasts made, and manage songs and playlists.
The tutor is told to reply in the language the learner writes in, in English when that is unclear, and to hold a conversation in Polish only when asked.

history.text: The tutor is told to reply in the language the learner writes in and to hold a conversation in Polish only when asked.
history.reason: The owner decided English is the default when the learner's language is not clear.

requirements.text: Replies stream in as they are generated and are rendered as Markdown built from elements, never from model-written markup; the one exception is mathematics, rendered to MathML with untrusted commands off.
What the tutor did in the app is stored with each message and given to later turns, and the reply shows buttons that open those things.
The tutor can read the learner's progress, the learning log's analysis and a lesson's mastery ledger through tools.
A reply is written by a background task and survives leaving the screen; one finished off screen arrives as a notification.
A reply cut off by the app closing is marked as interrupted, with a button to ask again.
The learner can keep several conversations, listed most recently used first, each with its own history and titled after its first question until renamed.
Deleting a conversation leaves everything the tutor made in the app in place.
An id of the wrong kind, or a made-up id, passed to a tool fails with a message saying what was expected, instead of acting on another row.
While a reply is being written on Android, the app is kept alive with a quiet notification.
